After over a decade of electrification in China's automotive market, with Huawei's five "realms" setting a precedent, how will the Qijing brand, a deep collaboration between Huawei and GAC, carve out its niche? At the Huawei Qiankun Ecosystem Conference on November 20, Qijing provided an answer. First and foremost is product definition, which determines the brand's development direction. Here, Qijing's choice is to "have it all"—creating vehicles that are safe, stylish, highly intelligent, and offer superior handling. 

Simultaneously, amid rapid AI advancements, Qijing has set its long-term vision as "shaping the mobile intelligent entity." Unlike traditional cars that passively respond to commands, it will actively perceive needs through in-vehicle sensors and home IoT devices, using AI models to make autonomous decisions and provide services. 

01 A "Mini-Huawei" Focused on Mobility: While the vision is ambitious, realizing it requires grounded efforts. To achieve Qijing's goals, Huawei not only empowers it with robust technology but also deeply integrates teams and processes, making Qijing essentially a "mini-Huawei" concentrated on mobility solutions. 

As the automotive industry enters the intelligent era, smart technology is key to differentiating products. Technologically, all Qijing models will feature the Huawei Qiankun suite, including Qiankun Intelligent Driving, Harmony Cockpit, Qiankun Vehicle Control, Qiankun In-Car Light, and Qiankun Vehicle Cloud. With the global tech community increasingly focused on physical world AI, the most critical component of the Huawei Qiankun suite is naturally Qiankun Intelligent Driving.
